Personally, I don?ôt mind the fragrance/ flavor, but I?ôve read too many articles cautioning against products that include it to give this five stars with its inclusion.I found myself using the product as a stand-alone gloss. The formula formed what felt like a cushiony, protective layer between my lips and the environment. The finish wasn?ôt sticky/tacky nor did it bleed. And although I was skeptical at first, the sheer, barely-there peach color is very attractive and I could see the color working on a variety of skin tones. I loved the way my lips looked with this on and the way they felt afterward. My male friends paid me many compliments.Application tip: the packaging is a little stiff, but if you gently squeeze while rubbing the applicator on your lips, you can limit the amount of product that comes out. column10: I live in Hawaii where the sun is intense and swimming is done in the ocean. The preservation of our islands is very important to us, and chemical sunscreens are polluting our beautiful beaches and snorkeling spots. For this reason, the state has banned the sale of oxybenzone and octinoxate, ingredients found in conventional chemical sunscreens that lead to coral bleaching. So naturally, I was in search of a reef safe sunscreen with a light weight formula for daily use. I soon learned that this is NOT the product I was looking for. While Supergoop?ôs formulas do not contain oxybenzone or octinoxate, they still contain chemicals such as avobenzone and octocrylene that have been found to be harmful to marine eco health as well. Plus, chemical sunscreens work by absorbing into the skin and have been linked to endocrine disruption and skin sensitivity. The gel went on light and matte upon first application, but there was a distinct acrid chemical smell that followed. The next day my skin, though not burnt, was rough dry and scaly. Mineral sunscreens that contain non-nano zinc oxide or non-nano titanium dioxide are generally recognized as the only safe and effective UVA / UVB protection that do no harm marine ecosystems. I?ôve since discovered there are many non-nano mineral sunscreens on the market with excellent light weight formulas that leave no white cast, are safe for your skin, and kind to our oceans. I wanted to share my findings, since this seems to be a popular sunscreen choice amongst Sephora shoppers. Great reviews, labeled clean and reef safe, reasons why you may consider purchasing this product and reasons that convinced me to give it a try as well. But upon further research, I realized Supergoop?ôs marketing is an example of greenwashing. Please be aware of buzzwords like ?úreef safe??and ?úclean??as there are no regulations for these labels, and they are often used to mislead consumers. A good reminder to research ingredients and shop mindfully.

column10: was excited at first. . .then i looked up the ingredients....here?ôs what i found.  Ôø?ÔøºWhat Is Avobenzone and Is It Safe In Sunscreen?Avobenzone was introduced in the 1990s and is a common chemical sunscreen. Unlike other chemical sunscreens that just protect from the sunburn-causing UVB rays, avobenzone also protects from UVA rays, the rays that cause premature aging and skin cancer. This chemical is given a two rating by theEWG. So what?ôs wrong with avobenzone? It seems like a safe sunscreen, right?ÔøºWhat?ôs wrong with avobenzone?Avobenzone, by itself, is relatively safe in terms of toxicity, but it breaks down quickly in the sun. Once exposed to the sun, avobenzone alone only offers about 30 minutes of protection.[i]Since UVA rays are the sneaky rays that do their damage deep within the layers of your skin, you wouldn?ôt even know it until many years later.Why is avobenzone used in sunscreen?So maybe you?ôre asking why they don?ôt they just use an ingredient that is better friends with the sunshine. We wish we knew! Because many chemical sunscreen companies still use avobenzone for UVA protection, they then have to add not-so-safe chemicals like octocrylene to make it work longer than 30 minutes.[ii]Octocrylene helps stabilize avobenzone, which is good, but it is a known endocrine disruptor that also releases free radicals.[iii]Not good. Skin sample tests showed there were more free radicals when using octocrylene than skin exposed to the sun with no sunscreen at all.[iv]And remember, free radicals, also known as reactive oxygen species (ROS), can damage skin cells and increase the risk for cancer and other health issues.[v]

column10: I live in Hawaii where the sun is intense and swimming is done in the ocean. The preservation of our islands is very important to us, and chemical sunscreens are polluting our beautiful beaches and snorkeling spots. For this reason, the state has banned the sale of oxybenzone and octinoxate, ingredients found in conventional chemical sunscreens that lead to coral bleaching. So naturally, I was in search of a reef safe sunscreen with a light weight formula for daily use. I soon learned that this is NOT the product I was looking for. While Supergoop?ôs formulas do not contain oxybenzone or octinoxate, they still contain chemicals such as avobenzone and octocrylene that have been found to be harmful to marine eco health as well. Plus, chemical sunscreens work by absorbing into the skin and have been linked to endocrine disruption and skin sensitivity. The gel went on light and matte upon first application, but there was a distinct acrid chemical smell that followed. The next day my skin, though not burnt, was rough dry and scaly. Mineral sunscreens that contain non-nano zinc oxide or non-nano titanium dioxide are generally recognized as the only safe and effective UVA / UVB protection that do no harm marine ecosystems. I?ôve since discovered there are many non-nano mineral sunscreens on the market with excellent light weight formulas that leave no white cast, are safe for your skin, and kind to our oceans. I wanted to share my findings, since this seems to be a popular sunscreen choice amongst Sephora shoppers. Great reviews, labeled clean and reef safe, reasons why you may consider purchasing this product and reasons that convinced me to give it a try as well. But upon further research, I realized Supergoop?ôs marketing is an example of greenwashing. Please be aware of buzzwords like ?úreef safe??and ?úclean??as there are no regulations for these labels, and they are often used to mislead consumers. A good reminder to research ingredients and shop mindfully.

column10: was excited at first. . .then i looked up the ingredients....here?ôs what i found.  Ôø?ÔøºWhat Is Avobenzone and Is It Safe In Sunscreen?Avobenzone was introduced in the 1990s and is a common chemical sunscreen. Unlike other chemical sunscreens that just protect from the sunburn-causing UVB rays, avobenzone also protects from UVA rays, the rays that cause premature aging and skin cancer. This chemical is given a two rating by theEWG. So what?ôs wrong with avobenzone? It seems like a safe sunscreen, right?ÔøºWhat?ôs wrong with avobenzone?Avobenzone, by itself, is relatively safe in terms of toxicity, but it breaks down quickly in the sun. Once exposed to the sun, avobenzone alone only offers about 30 minutes of protection.[i]Since UVA rays are the sneaky rays that do their damage deep within the layers of your skin, you wouldn?ôt even know it until many years later.Why is avobenzone used in sunscreen?So maybe you?ôre asking why they don?ôt they just use an ingredient that is better friends with the sunshine. We wish we knew! Because many chemical sunscreen companies still use avobenzone for UVA protection, they then have to add not-so-safe chemicals like octocrylene to make it work longer than 30 minutes.[ii]Octocrylene helps stabilize avobenzone, which is good, but it is a known endocrine disruptor that also releases free radicals.[iii]Not good. Skin sample tests showed there were more free radicals when using octocrylene than skin exposed to the sun with no sunscreen at all.[iv]And remember, free radicals, also known as reactive oxygen species (ROS), can damage skin cells and increase the risk for cancer and other health issues.[v]
